$comment: The Bloom language, as data: its token scales, colour roles, modifier rules, layering and environment.
scripts/generate.mjs turns this file into the runtime tables (src/generated/spec.generated.ts),
the web stylesheet (src/generated/web-sheet.generated.ts) and the compiler tables
Every value here is a Bloom rung: src/__tests__/spec.test.ts holds each one equal to Bloom.

Navigation (packages/bloom-language/src/router): appLayout, navStack, route and tabView are drawn by layout(); the screen modifiers in universal (title … onReselect) are read from the root of a screen() body and draw nothing elsewhere.

length.$comment: A frame's length relative to its parent (Tailwind's w-full, w-1/2…): the parent's width or height times the fraction; fit is its content's width (w-fit: fit-content), up to what the parent has.

zIndex.$comment: Bloom's Z_INDEX (styles/z-index.ts): the stacking levels its own components use; the numeric ones are Tailwind's own z-20, z-30 and z-50 and the exact levels apps write in two or more places (z-[2], z-[60]), each its value.

shadow.$comment: Bloom's elevation roles (design-tokens/shadows.ts): the web box-shadow of each; native draws bloomShadowStyle(role). The rest are Tailwind's own shadows (shadow-2xs … shadow-2xl), each named by its exact box-shadow, drawn as that box-shadow on every platform.

scale.$comment: How much a view is scaled where it is laid out: Bloom's own factors (PressableScale's pressed 0.98, the engagement pop's dip 0.7 and swell 1.2, full 1), then exact factors carried over from apps, named by their percent (Tailwind's scale-105 is '105').

rotation.$comment: Degrees: Bloom's own turns, then the exact angle apps write in two or more places, named by its degrees (Tailwind's rotate-45 is '45').

colors.$comment: role: [ThemeColors key (native paint), canonical CSS variable without -- (web)]; a colour the same in every theme (white, black, transparent) gives the colour itself for the web.

$comment: How each material draws on each platform. sheen, fill, tintOpacity: Bloom Surface (the web, and native where the platform glass is absent); fill is the colour role it paints from when untinted (null: Surface keeps its own fill), tintOpacity the glassOpacity a tint takes by default (null: the colour as it is).
lensBlur: the lens engine's frost (Android and OxyOS), a multiplier of the engine's own. iosStyle: the glassEffect style (iOS 26).

toneRole.$comment: The colour role a solid control of each Bloom tone fills with: an untinted glass under a solid Button or FAB takes it as its tint (null: the glass stays neutral).

objects.$comment: The object parameters: the keys each takes, and the token set of every value.

$comment: when(condition, v => v…): the modifiers inside override the values the chain set before it, while the condition holds.

modifiers: what a variant can change (style only). On the web a live condition is CSS over the generated sheet's classes; native reads it from the environment (the window's breakpoint, the theme, the view's own press host).
disabled and the platforms are known when the view renders: a variant under one is applied or dropped then.
when: a variant inside a variant holds while both conditions do (md and hovered: `when('md', v => v.when('hovered', …))`).

selectors.$comment: The web selector of each scheme and state condition, & standing for the class it styles. A breakpoint is a min-width media query at its breakpoint rung. The anchor class blsg is on the view's outermost box, and a state is that of the element's NEAREST anchor (itself or the closest box around it), as native's leaves read the nearest press host: an outer view's state never reaches an inner view's variants. A state is the innermost pressable's, as react-native-web's Pressable takes it (a hover or press inside an inner one is not the outer one's): the state's anchor has no pressable in the same state inside it (:has; blsp is the class a pressable react-native-web draws carries: the language's own hosts and Bloom's Avatar and EngagementAction, @oxy.so/bloom/styles PRESS_HOST_CLASS), and the class is in that anchor with no anchor between. The :where() parts add no specificity: a state's rule stays two classes over the base, the scheme's one.

easing.$comment: Bloom's curves (EASING in @oxy.so/bloom/motion), cubic-beziers by name; spec.test.ts holds them equal.

motion.$comment: Bloom's motion table (MOTION in @oxy.so/bloom/motion) by name, the timings Bloom's own animations play: { duration, easing } (an easing above) or a spring { response, dampingRatio }. spec.test.ts holds this table equal to Bloom's.

environment.$comment: The text and icon traits a view hands everything inside it, and what each is when nothing sets it. fontSize is the size of a Bloom Text with no variant, which a leading or a tracking measures from when no font is set.

modifiers.$comment: name: parameter types, in order. A trailing ? is optional; padding takes (value) or (edge, value). motionValue: a MotionValue (useMotionValue); scale, offset and rotation take one in place of a token.
label: value
title: value
subtitle: value

nodes.$comment: kind: { constructors, own modifiers beyond the universal ones (universal: false takes only its own), the token sets its size(), tint(), style() and shape() read }

$comment: A Bloom icon's SF Symbol: what iOS's own components (the tab bar, the navigation bar's items, system menus) draw for it.

scripts/generate.mjs checks that each icon is a Bloom icon and each symbol an SF Symbol. An icon with no symbol draws no glyph in a system component; a toolbar item whose glyph has none stays Bloom's own view.
